title: A global complete intersection has the expected dimension at every point
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $m,t\ge0$ integers, $Q=k[y_1,\dots,y_m]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f_1,\dots,f_t\in Q$ and $T=Q/(f_1,\dots,f_t)$. Assume $T\neq0$ and that the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is $\dim T=m-t$. Then for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset T$ the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ at the point $\mathfrak p$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is $\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}T)=m-t$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00S8 (section-lci, line 35806), the paragraph following Definition 00S9 (definition-lci-field, line 35817), lines 35834-35849: 'we conclude that dim(S_m) = n - c for all maximal ideals of S and that Spec(S) is equidimensional of dimension n - c, see Lemma 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field)', with Lemma 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Lemma 00KW (lemma-one-equation); used in the proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), last paragraph ('t = m - dim(S_g)')

proof.text: The upper bound follows directly from the infimum defining local dimension: the whole spectrum is an open neighbourhood, and its dimension is the assumed value.
Apply the lower-bound theorem at the chosen prime and combine the two inequalities by antisymmetry.
